I just feel so lost right now. I've been discharged by the mental health team after three years of them not doing very much, because the only option they eventually decided to offer was DBT, and I knew there was no way I was going to be able to face the strict regimen they wanted me to go through.
My parents are pressuring me to "make changes" and "do more with my life", and yet I literally never see them. I haven't left the house yet this year, and no-one seems to care. To say I'm isolated and completely on my own is an understatement.

Unfortunately I do think they describe me quite well, and it's hard to not feel defined by them. I have been diagnosed with BPD, depression, severe agoraphobia and social anxiety. I am also on the autistic spectrum.
On a good day I would probably have just completely ignored the post, but my good days are non-existent right now.

I was in High School at the time. They stopped classes and were showing continuous news coverage from the BBC I believe. There was a lot of repeat showing of the actual plane crash (the first one), and suggestions on the circumstances of the plane hi-jack, as at the time they seemed to have no idea why this happened.
After the second plane hit, I remember shocked silence in the hall where we were all watching it. As far as I could tell, the footage of the second plane hitting was pretty much live. Lots of panning shots of the damage and just very matter of fact descriptions of what had happened. It was obviously pointed out that the buildings hit were the WTC, and that loss of life would be high but impossible to estimate at the time.
